data.narrative:
Radiant, a Series D nuclear energy company founded by Doug Bernauer, has raised $465M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 10 nuclear energy firms: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The stage-progression method is applicable here, using the last post-money valuation of $1.0B as a baseline and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, yielding $1.5B. The peer-median method is not applicable: while 6 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), with zero matches across these refined buckets. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the specialized nature of nuclear energy development and capital requirements.

The triangulated range is $1.3B to $1.7B, with a median of $1.5B, derived from the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the limited dataset for stage-progression anchoring and the absence of narrow peer comparables to validate or adjust the stage-based multiple. Capital efficiency metrics, technology maturation milestones, and regulatory progress would refine this estimate materially if available.
